paths.description: Redirected landing page and primary service navigation; represents the portal homepage and global gov.br chrome.
Technical-documentation listing; represents the library/listing template.
Current DANFSE news item; represents the article/content template.
Public invoice consultation form; represents the primary unauthenticated transactional flow and invalid-submit state.
Deliberately missing route; represents HTTP/navigation recovery.

findings.summary: The cookie consent layer obscures the primary content on every gov.br template tested.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360 px screenshots show a fixed, dimming consent layer covering roughly half the viewport before any interaction; on mobile it blocks the article and primary service cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent notice for non-essential cookies and preserve immediate access to core content, following light-dismiss guidance.

findings.summary: The blocking cookie layer is a custom fixed div rather than a semantic dialog or popover.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found one full-width fixed .br-cookiebar but zero dialog, popover, or details elements; screenshots show modal-like behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the consent surface with a semantic dialog/popover pattern, focus management, Escape/light dismiss where appropriate, and an accessible name.

findings.summary: The portal does not adapt its visual theme to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot remains the same white/light-blue theme as the default, and the DOM/CSS probe found no adaptive dark surface behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define dark surface, text, border, and image treatments with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Long portal pages provide no scroll-progress or scroll-state-aware navigation cue.
findings.evidence: The 5,474 px mobile homepage uses conventional static chrome; the platform probe found no scroll-timeline rules and screenshots show no progress or section cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained scroll-progress or section-state affordance on long content, while honoring reduced motion.

findings.summary: Primary page/state changes do not use view transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero view-transition rules and the MPA navigation has no transition affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with cross-document view transitions, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The public consultation form does not expose native required-state or usable invalid-submit feedback.
findings.evidence: All business fields report required=false despite visible asterisks; clicking submit at 360 px leaves the page at the form/captcha with no visible field-specific errors in the captured state.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark required controls with required/aria-required, validate after interaction, place specific errors beside fields, announce an error summary, and move focus to it.

findings.summary: Homepage loading is very slow and transfers 13.4 MB, mostly oversized PNG imagery.
findings.evidence: Trace measured FCP 5.69 s and LCP 12.03 s; Lighthouse measured mobile LCP 23.3 s with performance 0.49; HAR recorded 13,419,727 transferred bytes, including 11,020,326 image bytes and individual PNGs up to 2.21 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Resize and transcode hero/news images, serve responsive sources, prioritize only the LCP image, lazy-load below-fold media, and consolidate render-blocking CSS/JS.

findings.summary: The homepage is not visually stable during a throttled mobile load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.144 and identified five layout-shift culprits, although the short post-load layout observer measured 0 after settling.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for banners, images, embeds, and late UI; use stable font fallbacks and avoid injecting chrome above existing content.

findings.summary: The page ships a fragmented, partly legacy resource graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 19 stylesheets, 28 scripts and 16 fonts; Lighthouse flagged three large first-party scripts without valid source maps; Swiper 3.4.2 is loaded from a third-party CDN.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit route-level usage, remove unused Plone bundles, consolidate critical styles, modernize legacy libraries, and publish valid production source maps where policy allows.

findings.summary: Interactive controls and links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found one unnamed button and seven links without discernible names, plus a visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch; the focus probe also recorded multiple visible links with empty text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon button and image/card link a programmatic name matching its visible purpose; remove empty duplicate links from the tab order.

findings.summary: The consultation form lacks basic document and form structure.
findings.evidence: The consultation probe found an empty html lang, zero headings, and no associated labels for the main text/select controls; its first visual content begins directly with a fieldset-like block.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="pt-BR", add one descriptive h1, use fieldset/legend for the query mode, and explicitly associate every label and error with its control.

findings.summary: The homepage has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The platform probe returned description:null and Lighthouse failed the meta-description SEO audit; article pages do include descriptions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, page-specific Portuguese meta description describing the NFS-e portal and its primary services.

findings.summary: Security policy headers are only partially defensive.
findings.evidence: The final gov.br document response includes HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, strict-origin-when-cross-origin and CSP frame-ancestors, but the CSP does not restrict script/style sources and no Permissions-Policy was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP covering script/style/connect/image sources and an explicit least-privilege Permissions-Policy while retaining HSTS and anti-framing controls.

findings.summary: The standalone consultation application does not declare its content language.
findings.evidence: The consultation DOM probe returned an empty html lang while the gov.br content templates correctly use pt-br.
findings.suggestedFix: Set html lang="pt-BR" and use logical CSS properties so future bidirectional/localized variants remain viable.

findings.summary: Consultation fields provide little browser-native input assistance.
findings.evidence: The consultation probe found empty autocomplete values on all business inputs, generic text input types, and no native required constraints.
findings.suggestedFix: Use appropriate inputmode/autocomplete tokens where standardized, constraints and examples for tax identifiers and invoice keys, without disabling paste.

findings.summary: Image delivery is far beyond a proportionate sustainability budget.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 11.02 MB to 16 images, with seven PNG/JPEG assets between 0.83 MB and 2.21 MB; total transfer is 13.42 MB for a mostly informational landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and responsive srcset/sizes, cap source dimensions to display needs, and enforce an image/page-weight budget in publishing.

findings.summary: Public service capabilities are not exposed in a structured agent-readable form.
findings.evidence: The DOM/probe found conventional HTML links/forms but no WebMCP registration or agentic tool metadata; the consultation is a meaningful public task that agents could assist with while preserving confirmation and captcha boundaries.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose safe, read-only discovery and form-assistance capabilities through progressive WebMCP/agentic-form metadata, requiring explicit user confirmation for submissions.

findings.summary: The page relies on a large third-party delivery footprint even before consent.
findings.evidence: Tracker/HAR capture found seven third-party origins and 84 of 86 requests classified cross-origin from the requested host, totaling 13.42 MB; no known analytics tracker was detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Self-host or consolidate stable assets where practical, defer optional cross-origin services until needed/consented, and document each third party’s data purpose.

findings.summary: Several primary interactive targets are smaller than recommended touch dimensions.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe measured the menu at 28×28 px and several social/icon links at roughly 19–33 px; mobile screenshots show dense floating accessibility controls over content.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44×44 CSS-pixel hit areas (or equivalent spacing) for primary icon controls and prevent floating utilities from covering content.

taskList.title: Optimize and budget responsive image delivery
Make the consultation form structurally accessible and recoverable
Remove unnamed and undersized interactive targets
Replace the blocking custom cookie layer with a semantic non-intrusive pattern
Reduce and modernize the CSS, JavaScript, font, and third-party graph
Strengthen CSP and least-privilege browser policies
Progressively expose safe agent-readable service capabilities
Add restrained modern navigation transitions and long-page state cues
